explanation: A declaration tells the compiler the name and type of an object or function. At a use of that name, the compiler needs a declaration visible at that point.
exampleExplanation: The first line declares points. The second line can use it because the declaration is already visible.
misconceptions: C identifiers are case-sensitive. points and Points are different names.
An undeclared-name diagnostic can come from a typo, a missing declaration, or a declaration that belongs to another scope.

reference.title: Local C reference on declarations
reference.text: A declaration supplies a type and a declarator, such as int score. A definition also provides an object or a function body. A prototype such as int total(int); declares a function and its parameter types. Headers can make declarations visible to more than one source file.
